s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation are present in the affected skin
Motion of the right limb joint is slightly limited
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings include normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion and histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive skin hardening with mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation, consistent with morphea

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin hardening and limited joint motion, although less specific than linear scleroderma

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality on MRI, with increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

shortlist.label: Stiff Skin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive skin hardening with limited joint motion, although rare and less likely than linear scleroderma or morphea

raw.rationale: The patient's unilateral skin hardening, mild hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation, along with the involvement of the right thigh and buttock, are characteristic of linear scleroderma. The histopathological findings of normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with well-defined, circular plaques, which is not consistent with the patient's ill-defined, stony-hard plaque.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a systemic disease that typically affects multiple areas of the body, whereas the patient's symptoms are unilateral and localized to the right thigh and buttock.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic fasciitis is characterized by rapid onset of skin thickening and inflammation, which is not consistent with the patient's 7-year history of progressive skin hardening and lack of inflammation on histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Stiff Skin Syndrome
rejected.why: Stiff skin syndrome is a rare disease that presents with diffuse skin thickening and stiffness, which is not consistent with the patient's localized and unilateral symptoms.
